title: Stars and the Origin of Elements
seo_title: Stars and Elements Worksheets: Fusion, Life Cycles, Supernovae and Spectra (Earth Science)
standard_text: Communicate scientific ideas about the way stars, over their life cycle, produce elements.
meta_desc: Free high school Earth and space science worksheets on stars and the origin of elements (NGSS HS-ESS1-3): fusion in stars, star life cycles, supernovae, spectra and star color. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Fusion builds elements up to iron; supernovae and neutron-star mergers make heavier ones.
body_html:
How to think about it

Stars make the elements, layer by layer.

  • Big Bang: hydrogen and helium. Ordinary stars: helium, then carbon and oxygen in red giants.
  • Massive stars fuse heavier elements up to iron. Heavier elements (gold, uranium) form in supernovae and neutron-star mergers.
  • Spectra reveal a star's elements; color shows temperature (blue hot, red cool).
Example

3 helium-4 nuclei fuse. Product?

3 × 2 = 6 protons

3 × 4 = 12

Answer: carbon-12

Example

Where was the gold on Earth made?

Heavier than iron

Answer: neutron-star mergers and supernovae

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all elements came from the Big Bang.
  • Thinking stars get energy by fusing iron.
  • Thinking red stars are the hottest.

faq.q: Where do the elements come from?
faq.a: Hydrogen and helium came from the Big Bang. Stars fused heavier elements up to iron. Elements heavier than iron came mostly from supernovae and neutron-star mergers.

faq.q: Why does fusion stop at iron?
faq.a: Fusing nuclei lighter than iron releases energy, but fusing iron uses energy, so a star's core cannot keep going.

faq.q: How do we know what stars are made of?
faq.a: Each element absorbs light at its own set of wavelengths, so the dark lines in a star's spectrum show which elements are present.
